title: Composing as a faker from old chord constructions
summary: Unable to read music, he built new tunes on chords of older pieces; the band were all fakers.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you, being a faker and not being able to line new tunes as fast as the people would...

I had to have something new tunes. So I'd take some of these old tunes like Shine on Harvest Moon. Take the chord construction. I made the jazz band ball out of it. I'd take old pieces like the Georgia Camp Meeting Ball. I made the fidgeted feet out of it. The last part I put on myself. But the rest of it are the same chord constructions. But you know, I played a little chords on the piano. And I understood it. Most old fakers you will find can play three or four instruments.

Yes, that we know. Now, Nick, let me clarify this. Because remember, you and I are talking as musicians. But the people who are listening to us don't know exactly what we mean. Out of the whole original jazz band that you had in Chicago and later in New York, the only one who could actually read music was the piano player, Russell Robinson.
Well, that came in later years after Ragus had died.
Yeah.
And we couldn't get a piano player. And Robinson had learned these tunes off the phonograph record. And he came to New York. And we had tried out so many piano players.
Mm-hmm.
We had Eddie Shields come up from New Orleans. And he couldn't fit in. We sent him back.
Well, in other words, originally none of the men could read music.
No, none of us read music. We were fakers.
Uh-huh.
And we understood one another. It was just like, I don't know, like you had a cogwheel. I was always one known to hit him. Then the way I was going.

That's a wonderful thing. Now, so in other words, you revised each of these tunes. And it was known among you fellas by a completely different name. Is that correct? That's correct. And that's a very interesting point. That's a story I've never heard before. That fidgety feet then was originally, you say.
It came. No, it wasn't originally. I get me wrong. I won't get no royalties on it.
No, I know what you mean.
I said I took the chord construction.
Yeah.
And on top of that, I'll...
You put your own...
Melody.
Well, you can't copyright a C chord. You know that, don't you? No, that's right. But I'm telling you, the melody's entirely different.
And that's where it came from.
Yes.
If anybody wants to look it up, all they got to do is compare them. And they'll see that I have told the truth.
